clue.text: Conflict at Lord's?

parts.note: a fierce set-to fought out on a prepared cricket strip at Lord's, the London cricket ground, between bats

explanation.surface: A dispute breaking out at a famous cricket ground.
explanation.walkthrough: Lord's is the London home of cricket; there the strip is the pitch and the players wield bats, so the pun pictures a full-scale fight there.
explanation.definitionFit: A set-piece clash between armies on chosen ground is a large formal conflict.

clue.text: Top 15 also perhaps for Stephen Foster's composition 1 10, 41

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Top 15 also perhaps for Stephen Foster's composition 1 10, 41 (10,4)': the OCR is garbled ('1 10, 41') and no wordplay for the answer can be recovered from it

clue.text: Make light of upset about Irishman

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means the pieces are turned over, read from bottom to top

parts.note: re is Latin-derived for about, concerning
Pat (Patrick) is the stock crossword Irishman

explanation.surface: Someone belittling a disturbance involving an Irishman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make light of' reads as 'belittle', but the definition is just 'light': a thin candle or spill.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin wax-coated wick used for lighting candles or fires is a kind of light.

clue.text: Form-fillers classed with Churchill, perhaps

parts.note: not people completing paperwork but pupils filling school forms (classes) at the same school Churchill attended

explanation.surface: Bureaucrats doing paperwork who rank alongside Churchill.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a school class; Winston Churchill was educated at Harrow, a famous English public school, so its pupils share that class with him.
explanation.definitionFit: Pupils or old boys of Harrow School are so named after the school.

clue.text: Picture of the Flying Doctor?

parts.note: an image or sketch, and also what a doctor does when pulling out teeth

explanation.surface: An image of the Australian air-ambulance medic.
explanation.walkthrough: A sketch is a picture, and a doctor extracting a tooth is said to be pulling or drawing it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sketch made with pencil or pen is a picture.

clue.text: Music composed by an old poet

parts.note: Dante Alighieri, the medieval Italian poet

explanation.surface: A piece written by an ancient bard.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece or movement played at a moderately slow walking pace is a musical term.

clue.text: Ronald's capital goes in river carrier

indicators.note: goes in tells us one piece is placed inside the river's name

parts.note: the Tay is the longest river in Scotland

indicators.note: capital here means the initial, upper-case letter of the name

explanation.surface: Ronald's money ends up in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' looks like money but means the first letter, R.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat board with a rim is used to carry plates and cups.

clue.text: Letters written on French milk rise appear necessary

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it

parts.note: the letters S and N spelt out as words

indicators.note: rise in a down clue means the word reads upwards

parts.note: lait is French for milk

explanation.surface: Some letters penned about rising French milk seem vital.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vital or indispensable is necessary.

clue.text: Players in tennis trial? No, a different sort 4

indicators.note: a different sort of these letters is a rearrangement of them

explanation.surface: Sportsmen at a tennis try-out who prove to be of another kind.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '4' is an OCR artefact in the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: Sportsmen chosen to represent their country are capped players.

clue.text: Wrecker of Edna's pram in Stalky & Co.?

indicators.note: a wrecker smashes things up, so the letters are broken and rebuilt

parts.note: the name with its S counted as a letter

explanation.surface: Who smashed Edna's baby carriage in a Kipling story?
explanation.walkthrough: Stalky & Co. is Kipling's school tale; the definition points at the symbol printed in its title.
explanation.definitionFit: The & symbol standing for 'and' appears in the book title.

clue.text: Crime for which an Ulster lawyer was beheaded

indicators.note: beheaded means the lawyer's surname loses its head, the first letter

parts.note: Edward Carson, the Dublin-born lawyer who led Ulster Unionism

explanation.surface: An Ulster barrister executed for some offence.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Carson was a famous barrister and Ulster Unionist leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Deliberately setting fire to property is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Trunk with twisted roots 13

indicators.note: twisted means the letters of the following word are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: A tree trunk with gnarled roots.
explanation.walkthrough: The stray '13' is an OCR artefact in the clue as held.
explanation.definitionFit: The human body without head or limbs is called the trunk.

clue.text: They provide good cheer in both hemispheres

parts.note: N and S, north and south

explanation.surface: Something offers comfort all over the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Pubs and hostelries offer food, drink and hospitality.

clue.text: Joint supporter in a humble petition

definitions.meaning: what one kneels on to plead humbly

explanation.definitionFit: The leg's middle hinge is a joint, and one kneels on it, so it bears the weight when begging humbly.

clue.text: The ruddy draught Keats mentioned !

parts.note: the 'blushful' fountain Keats longs for in Ode to a Nightingale, a beaker full of the warm South

explanation.surface: A red drink named in a Romantic poem.
explanation.walkthrough: In Ode to a Nightingale Keats wishes for 'the true, the blushful' spring of the Muses; the '!' is the setter's.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring on Mount Helicon sacred to the Muses is the poetic draught Keats calls blushful.

clue.text: Browning work gave some pain ?

parts.note: both the business of turning hides or skin brown and a thrashing that hurt

explanation.surface: Reading Robert Browning's poetry was a bit painful.
explanation.walkthrough: Browning looks like the poet; it is making leather or skin brown, and the word also means a beating.
explanation.definitionFit: Curing hides into leather or bronzing skin in the sun is browning work, and a thrashing is a hiding.

clue.text: Snappish refusals ?

parts.note: both curt answers of no and the films produced by snapshots

explanation.surface: Curt, irritable ways of saying no.
explanation.walkthrough: Snappish suggests irritable, but it means belonging to snaps (photographs), whose film images come out reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: Answers of no are refusals, and developed film from photographs gives reversed images.

clue.text: Structural materials In cargo

indicators.note: the materials of the cargo are taken as raw letters to be reshaped

explanation.surface: Building materials carried in a ship's hold.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to the organs or to the basic make-up of something, organic means structural.

clue.text: Shakespearian character has a little party in prison

indicators.note: in places the small party inside the jail

parts.note: can is slang for jail
Lib, short for the Liberals, a small political party

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare figure throws a small party in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'party' is political, LIB for Liberal, not a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: The monster in The Tempest is a figure from Shakespeare.

clue.text: One of two play bouses cursed by Mercutio

definitions.text: One of two play bouses cursed by Mercutio

parts.words: One of two play bouses cursed by Mercutio
parts.note: the dying Mercutio cries 'A plague on both your houses' at the two feuding families of Romeo and Juliet

explanation.surface: Mercutio damned a pair of theatres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play houses' suggests theatres; here they are the feuding families in Romeo and Juliet.
explanation.definitionFit: Juliet's family is one of the two feuding houses of Verona.

clue.text: Out of which a horse bolts

definitions.text: Out of which a horse bolts

parts.words: Out of which a horse bolts
parts.note: a bolting horse is said to be out of this, that is no longer restrained

explanation.surface: A horse escaping from somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a stable or gate, but the phrase is 'out of ...' meaning unrestrained.
explanation.definitionFit: A runaway horse is beyond restraint, out of the rider's command.

clue.text: Declines to appear in lots of games

definitions.meaning: goes down, as the sun does
groups of games, as in tennis

explanation.definitionFit: The sun going down sinks, and a tennis match is played in groups of games.

clue.text: Sweet dish many put in the cooler

indicators.note: put in places the Roman numeral inside the cooling device

parts.note: a fan cools the air
L is the Roman numeral 50, a large number

explanation.surface: A dessert, lots of which are chilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cooler' suggests a fridge or a prison; it is a fan.
explanation.definitionFit: An open pastry case with a filling is a tart-like pudding.

clue.text: Nothing accounts for the backwardness of this tropical tree

indicators.note: backwardness means the pieces are read in reverse

parts.note: O, the zero
a/c twice, a plural of account

explanation.surface: Nothing explains why this tropical tree is so backward.
explanation.definitionFit: The tree whose beans give cocoa and chocolate grows in the tropics.

clue.text: Split about nothing with an oil-supplier

parts.note: c, circa, about
love is zero in tennis

explanation.surface: Breaking up over nothing with someone who supplies oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The tail 'with an oil-supplier' is a second hint: the spice clove gives clove oil.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of cleave, to divide, means split.

clue.text: E. European back in medieval Saxony

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An Eastern European returns to medieval Saxony.
explanation.definitionFit: A Pole, Czech or Russian belongs to the Slavonic peoples of Eastern Europe.

clue.text: Ivor's first book

indicators.note: first means just the opening part of the surname is kept

parts.note: Ivor Novello, the Welsh composer and actor

explanation.surface: Ivor's debut publication.
explanation.walkthrough: Ivor Novello was a Welsh songwriter and matinee idol; the first five letters of his surname make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long work of prose fiction is a book.

clue.text: Nutty Spanish port?

parts.note: a Catalan city that gives its name to a kind of hazelnut

explanation.surface: A crazy harbour town in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: Nutty seems to mean mad, but the city gives its name to a hazelnut.
explanation.definitionFit: The Catalan capital is a major Mediterranean seaport, and Barcelona nuts are hazelnuts.

clue.text: Youths at Ephesus employed on railway?

definitions.text: Youths at Ephesus employed on railway?

parts.words: Youths at Ephesus employed on railway?
parts.note: the legendary young men walled in a cave at Ephesus, pictured as wooden track supports

explanation.surface: Young men of Ephesus working on the railways.
explanation.walkthrough: The legend tells of seven Christian youths who slept for centuries in a cave near Ephesus; British railway ties are called sleepers.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary seven youths of Ephesus slept for about two centuries.
